title: Fix a token module that trusts unverified payloads
problem: A security review found two problems in tokens.py: the signing secret is hardcoded, and decode_access_token reads the payload without verifying anything, so anyone can write role: admin into a token. Make signing_secret read the secret from the environment and fail closed, and make decode_access_token verify the signature, algorithm, expiry, audience, issuer and required claims.
requirements: Edit only tokens.py. Don't change test_tokens.py
signing_secret reads os.environ[SECRET_ENV] on every call and raises RuntimeError when it's missing or shorter than MIN_SECRET_BYTES bytes
decode_access_token passes the secret, algorithms=[ALGORITHM], audience=AUDIENCE and issuer=ISSUER to jwt.decode, and requires exp, iat, sub, iss and aud
decode_access_token doesn't catch PyJWT's exceptions: callers handle jwt.InvalidTokenError
create_access_token keeps its claims; it uses signing_secret()
contract: signing_secret() -> str; create_access_token(user_id: int, role: str, expires_in: timedelta = 15 min) -> str; decode_access_token(token: str) -> dict (raises jwt.InvalidTokenError subclasses)
expectedBehavior: A token made by create_access_token decodes to its claims; a token with a changed payload, another key, alg none, a past exp, another audience or issuer, or without exp or sub raises jwt.InvalidTokenError; with CHAT_JWT_SECRET unset, both functions raise RuntimeError
edgeCases: The secret is rotated between creating and decoding a token
The environment variable is set but too short
A token whose header says alg: none
A correctly signed token for another audience
hints: Conceptual: the payload of a JWT is only base64, readable and writable by anyone. The signature is the only thing that makes it trustworthy, and only if the server checks it with a key it chose, an algorithm it chose, and claims it expects. Reading claims before that check is reading attacker input.

Specific: signing_secret uses os.environ.get(SECRET_ENV, "") and checks the length of the encoded bytes. jwt.decode needs the key, algorithms= as a list, audience=, issuer= and options={"require": [...]}. Expiry is checked automatically when exp is present; require makes it mandatory.

Implementation: delete SECRET. In signing_secret, raise RuntimeError(...) if len(secret.encode("utf-8")) < MIN_SECRET_BYTES, else return it. In decode_access_token return jwt.decode(token, signing_secret(), algorithms=[ALGORITHM], audience=AUDIENCE, issuer=ISSUER, options={"require": ["exp", "iat", "sub", "iss", "aud"]}).
evaluation: No secret value anywhere in the code; missing configuration stops the app instead of falling back
algorithms is a fixed list chosen by the server, never read from the token
You can explain how the starter's decode let a user become admin
